newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Intel upbeat on new high-speed chip.
newsitem.headline: Intel upbeat on new high-speed chip.

text.p: Intel Corp promised on Tuesday to stand behind its new Pentium microprocessor if it turned out to have a glitch or "errata" like the one that bedevilled its first generation Pentium.
"We've got our folks looking at it. If it's in fact real errata, we'll just follow the procedure we adopted (in 1994)", Intel chief operating officer and president-elect Craig Barrett told Reuters.
He was speaking after the launch of Intel's new Pentium II microprocessor -- microprocessors are the heart of a personal computer.
"We'll look seriously at it, figure out what it is, (and) stand behind our product," Barrett said.
Intel officials had earlier said they were looking into unconfirmed reports of "errata", a so-called floating point glitch that could cause computational errors.

"I think we're still the only computer company that publishes errata from our processors," Barrett said. "We'll publish it, (and) work with the computer manufacturers and software people to look for solutions."
Intel, the world's largest chip maker, on Wednesday launched its speedy new Pentium II processor, which has speeds of 300 megaherz (MHz), 266 MHz and 233 MHz units.
